text:
The loudest story in Philadelphia is Matvei Michkov's ice time. The New York Times asked it straight out, "Does Matvei Michkov deserve more ice time?", after a weekend of headlines about Michkov sending a message to the coaching staff. Our numbers make his case: the line of Noah Cates, Michkov and Porter Martone has taken 61 percent of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) in its minutes, the best of the Flyers' regular lines. He answered Monday with an assist and the first star in a 3-1 win in Vancouver.

The bigger picture is grim. Rick Tocchet's team is 5-10-5 with 15 points and takes only 43.7 percent of the expected goals, 42 percent at five on five. This isn't bad luck, mostly: our numbers say they've earned only about two more points than they have. They've also scored 8.76 fewer goals than their chances deserve. Our simulations give them a 3 percent playoff chance and project about 76 points.

Travis Konecny is back from injury, and Travis Sanheim anchors both of the top defensive pairs, first with Jamie Drysdale and then with Oliver Bonk. What to watch: whether the Michkov line gets more of the minutes, and whether a team this far back starts giving its young players the ice. Monday's third period, when Vancouver took over, showed how little margin there is.
headline: Michkov's minutes, and a season slipping away
